subject: Technical intake: dedicated pool requirements & scheduling
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike O'Leary <mike@fintronics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Technical intake: dedicated pool requirements & scheduling

Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposal for next steps so we can size a dedicated pool that meets Fintronics' production goals.

Recap / what we heard
- Primary use: customer-facing chat + contextual embeddings for search/rerank (mixed small/medium prompt lengths).
- Expected steady-state: ~40–60 QPS of small-to-medium generations (under 256 tokens) during business hours.
- Peak bursts: short spikes to ~120 QPS for 5–10 minute windows (marketing campaigns).
- Quality/latency target: p95 generation latency target ~200ms (lower preferred for chat).
- Cost sensitivity: must balance unit cost; open to quantized model variants or batching.

What we need before the sizing call
- Traffic sample (CSV or sample logs) showing request size distribution, tokens per request, and concurrency by minute.
- Top 10 representative prompts + percent of traffic for each.
- Any hard SLAs or retention constraints (audit/compliance notes).

Proposed next step
- 60-minute dedicated sizing/technical deep-dive with engineering + SRE from your side, and our runtime + solutions engineers on ours. We'll walk through: workload profile, target SLOs, model variant tradeoffs, and an initial GPU pool recommendation.

Times I can propose (PST):
- Tue May 4 — 9:00am, 11:30am, 3:00pm
- Wed May 5 — 10:00am, 1:30pm

Please pick one that works or suggest alternatives. I attached: discovery-notes (short call notes) and a traffic-sample-template.csv to make it easier to share the data.

Thanks — we want to make sure the sizing call is productive (we'll bring pre-flight questions based on the sample).

Best,

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: discovery-notes-20270502.pdf, traffic-sample-template.csv
From: Mike O'Leary <mike@fintronics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: sre-ops@fintronics.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Technical intake: dedicated pool requirements & scheduling

Soojin —

Appreciate the clear recap, that's exactly what we wanted. Quick answers and a time preference below.

Current clarifications
- The 40–60 QPS steady-state is accurate; our current spike patterns have reached ~110 QPS in the last quarter.
- Our target p95 is ideally <= 150–200ms for short responses; longer generation windows for few-shot prompts can tolerate higher latency.
- Cost is a constraint: we prefer recommendations that include a lower-cost quantized option for non-critical paths.
- Compliance: logs need to be retained 90 days and accessible to our audit team (we'll share the policy doc).

Attached: fintronics-qps.csv (5 weeks of minute-by-minute), hope it helps.

Preferred time: Tue May 4 at 11:30am PST works best for our SRE and platform reps. If that slot is still open on your side, lock it.

Also looping in our SRE alias above so they can add any topology/network constraints before the call.

Thanks,

Mike O'Leary
Head of Platform Engineering | Fintronics
mike@fintronics.com | +1 617-555-0987

Attachment: fintronics-qps.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical intake: dedicated pool requirements & scheduling

Mike —

11:30am PST on Tue May 4 is confirmed on our side. Sending a calendar invite from my calendar in a moment — please accept when you see it.

Who will join from Fintronics? Our suggested attendee list: one SRE/infra lead, one product/owner for workload questions, and any security/compliance contact who can speak to retention. From Redwood we'll have: Soojin (solutions), Priyom (runtime engineer), and me (systems/architecture).

Pre-call artifacts / agenda (attached as sizing-agenda.docx and linked in the invite):
- 0–10m: Introductions and desired outcomes
- 10–25m: Workload profile + traffic walk-through (you drive here)
- 25–45m: Latency/cost tradeoffs and recommended pool topology (kernels, GPU counts, quantization)
- 45–55m: Networking, TLS, and retention/audit considerations
- 55–60m: Next steps + timeline (POC, invoice/contract path if agreed)

One ask before the call: can your SRE add any egress/topology constraints (firewalls, proxies, internal NAT) to the shared Drive link? That way we can call out any network-related blockers during the meeting.

I'll include a short set of notes in the calendar invite and a link to the HubSpot deal. Looking forward to it.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
